notes.definition: Reproductive hormones control puberty and the menstrual cycle. Oestrogen (from the ovaries) and testosterone (from the testes) cause secondary sex characteristics, while FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone control egg maturation, ovulation and the uterus lining.
explanation: During puberty, reproductive hormones cause secondary sex characteristics to develop. In girls the main reproductive hormone is oestrogen, which is produced in the ovaries. At puberty eggs begin to mature, and one egg is released from an ovary approximately every 28 days. This release is called ovulation. In boys the main reproductive hormone is testosterone, which is produced by the testes and stimulates sperm production.

The menstrual cycle is a monthly cycle of about 28 days. It prepares the uterus to receive a fertilised egg. At the start of the cycle (about days 1 to 4) the uterus lining breaks down and is lost: this is menstruation, or a period. The lining then builds up again, an egg is released around day 14, and the lining is maintained in case a fertilised egg implants.

Several hormones are involved. Follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) causes an egg to mature in the ovary. Luteinising hormone (LH) stimulates the release of the egg (ovulation). Oestrogen and progesterone are involved in building up and maintaining the uterus lining. FSH and LH are released by the pituitary gland in the brain; oestrogen and progesterone are released by the ovaries.

Higher tier: these hormones interact. FSH from the pituitary causes an egg to mature and stimulates the ovaries to produce oestrogen. Rising oestrogen makes the lining thicken, inhibits FSH release (so no more eggs mature) and stimulates the pituitary to release LH. A surge of LH around day 14 triggers ovulation.

Higher tier: after ovulation the ovary produces progesterone. Progesterone maintains the thick uterus lining and inhibits the release of both FSH and LH. If the egg is not fertilised, progesterone levels fall. The lining then breaks down (menstruation), and because progesterone no longer inhibits the pituitary, FSH rises again and a new cycle begins.

You may be asked to extract and interpret data from graphs of hormone levels. Look for the LH peak (ovulation follows shortly after), the oestrogen peak just before it, and progesterone being high in the second half of the cycle while the lining is maintained.
keyFacts: Reproductive hormones cause secondary sex characteristics to develop at puberty.
Oestrogen is the main female reproductive hormone, produced in the ovaries.
Testosterone is the main male reproductive hormone, produced by the testes; it stimulates sperm production.
Ovulation is the release of an egg, approximately every 28 days.
FSH causes an egg to mature in the ovary.
LH stimulates the release of the egg (ovulation).
Oestrogen and progesterone build up and maintain the uterus lining.
FSH and LH are made by the pituitary gland; oestrogen and progesterone by the ovaries.
Higher: oestrogen inhibits FSH and stimulates LH; progesterone inhibits FSH and LH.
Higher: falling progesterone causes the lining to break down (menstruation).

keyTerms.definition: The stage when reproductive hormones cause secondary sex characteristics to develop and the body becomes able to reproduce.
The release of a mature egg from an ovary, approximately every 28 days.
The breakdown and loss of the uterus lining at the start of the menstrual cycle (a period).
Hormone from the pituitary gland that causes an egg to mature in the ovary.
Hormone from the pituitary gland that stimulates the release of an egg.
Main female reproductive hormone, made in the ovaries; builds up the uterus lining.
Hormone made by the ovaries after ovulation that maintains the uterus lining.
Main male reproductive hormone, made by the testes; stimulates sperm production.

workedExamples.title: Finding the day of ovulation
workedExamples.question: Ovulation usually happens about 14 days before the next period starts. A woman has a regular 32-day cycle. On which day of her cycle does she ovulate?
steps: The next period starts on day 32 + 1 = day 33 (day 1 of the next cycle).
Counting 14 days back from the end of the cycle: 32 − 14 = 18.

workedExamples.title: Reading a hormone graph (Higher)
workedExamples.question: A graph shows LH at 10 units on day 12, 70 units on day 14 and 15 units on day 16. Progesterone is low until day 15 then rises to a peak on day 21. Identify when ovulation happens and explain the progesterone change.
steps: The sharp LH peak (surge) is on day 14.
LH stimulates release of the egg, so ovulation happens at about day 14.
After ovulation the ovary produces progesterone, so progesterone rises from day 15.
Progesterone maintains the uterus lining and inhibits FSH and LH, which is why LH falls again.
workedExamples.answer: Ovulation is about day 14; progesterone rises afterwards to maintain the lining.

workedExamples.title: Percentage change in a hormone
workedExamples.question: LH rises from 5 units to 60 units. Calculate the percentage increase.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the menstrual cycle starts with ovulation.
misconceptions.right: In fact day 1 is the first day of menstruation (the period). Ovulation is around day 14 in a 28-day cycle.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think LH makes the egg mature.
misconceptions.right: In fact FSH causes an egg to mature; LH stimulates its release.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think FSH and LH are made by the ovaries.
misconceptions.right: In fact FSH and LH are made by the pituitary gland and travel in the blood to the ovaries. The ovaries make oestrogen and progesterone.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think progesterone causes menstruation.
misconceptions.right: In fact it is a fall in progesterone that causes the uterus lining to break down. High progesterone maintains the lining.

realWorld: Ovulation test kits detect the LH surge in urine, helping couples identify the most fertile days.
Hormonal contraceptives and fertility treatments work by changing the levels of these same hormones.
Period-tracking apps estimate ovulation by assuming it occurs about 14 days before the next period.
higherTier: Explain the interactions of FSH, oestrogen, LH and progesterone in the control of the menstrual cycle.
FSH stimulates the ovaries to produce oestrogen. Oestrogen inhibits FSH and stimulates LH release.
LH stimulates ovulation. Progesterone, from the ovary after ovulation, maintains the lining and inhibits FSH and LH.
Extract and interpret data from graphs showing hormone levels during the menstrual cycle.
examTips: Learn a table of each hormone: where it is made, and what it does. Most marks come from matching these correctly.
Use 'stimulates' and 'inhibits' precisely in Higher questions on interactions, and name the target (pituitary, ovary or uterus lining).
On graphs, ovulation is just after the LH peak. Quote the day from the graph and refer to the hormone level as evidence.
Write 'egg matures' for FSH and 'egg is released' for LH. Mixing these two up is the most common error.
summary: Reproductive hormones cause secondary sex characteristics at puberty.
Oestrogen comes from the ovaries; testosterone from the testes and stimulates sperm production.
An egg is released approximately every 28 days (ovulation).
FSH matures an egg; LH triggers its release.
Oestrogen and progesterone build up and maintain the uterus lining.
Higher: oestrogen inhibits FSH and stimulates LH; progesterone inhibits FSH and LH.

questions.question: Where is oestrogen mainly produced?
markScheme: 1 mark: Ovaries
questions.explanation: Oestrogen is the main female reproductive hormone and is made in the ovaries. The pituitary makes FSH and LH. The uterus is a target, not a source.

questions.question: What is the main male reproductive hormone?
markScheme: 1 mark: Testosterone
questions.explanation: Testosterone is produced by the testes and stimulates sperm production. Oestrogen and progesterone are female reproductive hormones.

questions.question: Which hormone causes an egg to mature in the ovary?
markScheme: 1 mark: FSH
questions.explanation: Follicle stimulating hormone causes egg maturation. LH causes release of the egg, and progesterone maintains the uterus lining.

questions.question: Which hormone stimulates the release of an egg from the ovary?
markScheme: 1 mark: LH
questions.explanation: A surge in LH around day 14 triggers ovulation. FSH matures the egg beforehand; oestrogen builds the lining.

questions.question: Which two hormones are involved in building up and maintaining the lining of the uterus?
markScheme: 1 mark: Oestrogen and progesterone
questions.explanation: Both are made by the ovaries and act on the uterus lining. FSH and LH from the pituitary act on the ovaries, not the lining.

questions.question: After puberty, approximately how often is an egg released from an ovary?
markScheme: 1 mark: Approximately every 28 days
questions.explanation: The menstrual cycle lasts about 28 days and one egg is released in each cycle, around day 14. Day 14 is the timing within the cycle, not the interval between eggs.

questions.question: Which gland secretes FSH and LH?
markScheme: 1 mark: Pituitary gland
questions.explanation: FSH and LH are made by the pituitary gland in the brain and carried in the blood to the ovaries, their target organ.

questions.question: During which days of a typical 28-day menstrual cycle does the uterus lining break down?
markScheme: 1 mark: Days 1 to 4
questions.explanation: By convention, day 1 is the first day of bleeding. The lining is built up afterwards, and is maintained from about day 14 to day 28.

questions.question: Which of these is a secondary sex characteristic caused by oestrogen during puberty?
markScheme: 1 mark: Development of breasts
questions.explanation: Breast development is caused by oestrogen. Facial hair and a deeper voice are caused by testosterone in boys. Sperm production is stimulated by testosterone.

questions.question: What effect does a high level of oestrogen have on the pituitary gland?
options: It stimulates FSH release and inhibits LH release
It stimulates both FSH and LH release
It inhibits FSH release and stimulates LH release
It inhibits both FSH and LH release
markScheme: 1 mark: It inhibits FSH release and stimulates LH release
questions.explanation: Inhibiting FSH stops more eggs maturing; stimulating LH leads to the LH surge and ovulation. Inhibiting both FSH and LH is the effect of progesterone.

questions.question: An egg is not fertilised. Progesterone levels fall at the end of the cycle. What is the effect?
options: The uterus lining breaks down and menstruation begins
markScheme: 1 mark: The uterus lining breaks down and menstruation begins
questions.explanation: Progesterone maintains the lining, so when it falls the lining is lost. The fall also removes inhibition of FSH so a new egg can start to mature, but ovulation does not happen immediately.

questions.question: Which hormones does progesterone inhibit?
markScheme: 1 mark: FSH and LH
questions.explanation: Progesterone acts on the pituitary to inhibit FSH and LH. This prevents another egg maturing and being released while the lining is maintained.

questions.question: Name the organ that produces testosterone and state one function of testosterone.
markScheme: 1 mark: testes
1 mark: stimulates sperm production (or causes male secondary sex characteristics)
questions.explanation: Testosterone is produced by the testes. The specification states it stimulates sperm production.

questions.question: What is meant by ovulation?
markScheme: 1 mark: the release of an egg from an ovary
questions.explanation: Ovulation is the release, not the maturation, of an egg. It happens around day 14 of a 28-day cycle.

questions.question: Describe the roles of FSH and LH in the menstrual cycle.
markScheme: 1 mark: FSH causes an egg to mature (in the ovary)
1 mark: LH stimulates the release of the egg / ovulation
questions.explanation: These two pituitary hormones act in order: first maturation (FSH), then release (LH). Mixing them up is the most common error.

questions.question: Explain why the uterus lining is maintained after ovulation.
markScheme: 1 mark: in case the egg is fertilised
1 mark: so a fertilised egg / embryo can implant (and develop) in the thick lining
questions.explanation: The thick lining, rich in blood vessels, is ready to receive an embryo. Progesterone maintains it. If fertilisation does not happen, it breaks down.

questions.question: FSH is a hormone. Name the gland that secretes FSH and the target organ that FSH acts on.
markScheme: 1 mark: pituitary gland
1 mark: ovary / ovaries
questions.explanation: FSH is released into the blood from the pituitary gland and carried to the ovaries, where it causes an egg to mature.

questions.question: Give two changes in boys at puberty that are caused by testosterone.
markScheme: 1 mark each, any two: sperm production starts; growth of facial or body hair; voice deepens; muscles develop; penis and testes enlarge
questions.explanation: Testosterone causes male secondary sex characteristics and stimulates sperm production.

questions.question: Explain how a rise in oestrogen leads to ovulation.
markScheme: 1 mark: oestrogen (high level) stimulates the pituitary gland
1 mark: to release LH (an LH surge)
1 mark: LH stimulates release of the egg / ovulation
questions.explanation: This is a positive link from ovary to pituitary to ovary. Oestrogen also inhibits FSH, which stops further eggs maturing, but that is not what triggers ovulation.

questions.question: Explain why FSH stays at a low level in the second half of the menstrual cycle.
markScheme: 1 mark: progesterone (and oestrogen) is high in the second half of the cycle
1 mark: it inhibits release of FSH from the pituitary gland
questions.explanation: Progesterone is produced by the ovary after ovulation. Its inhibition of FSH prevents another egg maturing while the lining is maintained.

questions.question: A graph shows LH levels in a woman's blood: day 10 = 8 units, day 12 = 20 units, day 14 = 65 units, day 16 = 10 units. Suggest the day on which ovulation happened. Give a reason using the data.
markScheme: 1 mark: day 14 (or just after day 14)
1 mark: LH is at its peak / surge (65 units) and LH stimulates release of the egg
questions.explanation: Ovulation follows the LH surge. Quoting the value from the data (65 units on day 14) is good practice in data questions.

questions.question: Ovulation usually happens about 14 days before the start of the next period. A woman has a regular 32-day menstrual cycle. On which day of her cycle would you expect ovulation?
markScheme: 1 mark: = day 18
questions.explanation: The 14 days after ovulation are fairly constant, so in a longer cycle ovulation happens later. 32 − 14 = 18. A common error is to assume day 14 or to halve 32 to get 16.

questions.question: One egg is released every 28 days. Calculate how many eggs are released in a year of 365 days. Give your answer as a whole number.
markScheme: 1 mark: 13 eggs
questions.explanation: 365 ÷ 28 = 13.04, so 13 complete cycles fit into a year. Rounding gives 13.

questions.question: A student records the length of five menstrual cycles: 27, 29, 28, 30 and 26 days. Calculate the mean cycle length.
markScheme: 1 mark: 140 ÷ 5 = 28 days
questions.explanation: Add the values and divide by the number of values. The mean of 28 days fits the typical cycle length.

questions.question: During a menstrual cycle, the concentration of LH in the blood rises from 5 units to 60 units. Calculate the percentage increase in LH.
markScheme: 1 mark: change = 60 − 5 = 55
questions.explanation: Percentage change uses the original value as the denominator. A common error is 60 ÷ 5 × 100 = 1200 %, which is the new value as a percentage of the old, not the increase.

questions.question: Describe the roles of hormones in controlling the menstrual cycle.
markScheme: Indicative content: FSH from the pituitary gland causes an egg to mature in the ovary; LH from the pituitary gland stimulates release of the egg (ovulation) around day 14; oestrogen from the ovaries builds up the uterus lining; progesterone from the ovaries maintains the uterus lining; the lining breaks down (menstruation) at the start of the cycle; the cycle lasts about 28 days.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): roles of all four hormones correctly described, with sources or timing.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or two roles correctly described.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Full marks need all four hormones matched to the correct role. Naming the gland that makes each one strengthens the answer.

questions.question: Describe how reproductive hormones cause changes in boys and girls during puberty.
markScheme: Indicative content: reproductive hormones cause secondary sex characteristics to develop; in girls, oestrogen is the main reproductive hormone and is produced in the ovaries; eggs begin to mature and one is released approximately every 28 days; menstrual cycle begins; breasts develop; in boys, testosterone is the main reproductive hormone and is produced by the testes; testosterone stimulates sperm production; voice deepens, facial and body hair grow.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): correct hormone and source for both sexes, with effects including egg release and sperm production.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): some correct effects or hormones for one sex.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Name the hormone, where it is made and what it does for each sex. Egg release and sperm production are the key specification points.

questions.question: Explain how the hormones FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone interact to control the menstrual cycle.
markScheme: Indicative content: FSH is released by the pituitary gland; FSH causes an egg to mature in the ovary; FSH stimulates the ovary to produce oestrogen; oestrogen causes the uterus lining to build up; oestrogen inhibits further release of FSH; oestrogen stimulates the pituitary to release LH; the LH surge stimulates ovulation around day 14; after ovulation the ovary produces progesterone; progesterone maintains the uterus lining; progesterone inhibits FSH and LH; if the egg is not fertilised progesterone falls; the lining breaks down (menstruation); FSH is no longer inhibited so it rises and the cycle restarts.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): detailed explanation of the interactions in a logical sequence, including inhibition and stimulation and why the cycle repeats.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): roles of most hormones with some interactions described.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): basic roles of hormones with no interactions.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: The command word 'explain' with 'interact' means you must say how each hormone affects the release of another, not just list roles. Follow the cycle in time order.
